chain.g: seventh degree or note of Guido of Arezzo's hexachordal scales

ety.text: From Middle English si (“seventh degree or note of Guido of Arezzo's hexachordal scales”), Italian si in the solmization of Guido of Arezzo, from the initials of Latin Sāncte Iohannēs (“Saint John (the Baptist)”) in the lyrics of the scale-ascending hymn Ut queant laxis by Paulus Deacon; thus, also an initialism of Sāncte Iohannēs.

senses.d: A syllable used in solfège to represent the seventh note of a major scale.

grp.label: seventh note of a major scale

chain.g: sacred, made inviolable, having been established as sacred.

ety.text: From Latin Sancte Iohannes (“Saint John”) in the hymn for St. John the Baptist.
